title: We’ll revamp flood action plan, says Najib | FMT
text:
We’ll revamp flood action plan, says Najib | FMT
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will consider flood disaster management in other countries as it conducts a review to improve the all-round operating procedure to tackle floods in the country.
“The review will look at improving the competency and leadership skills of personnel at all levels, the flood early warning system, the procurement of search and rescue vehicles and flood mitigation measures,” said Prime Minister Najib Razak here yesterday.
Najib said the government was also looking at the best flood management models used by others nations, reports The Star Online.
Deputy Prime Minister Muhyiddin Yassin, the chairman of the National Disaster Committee who is on a visit to Japan, said in Tokyo yesterday that Malaysia would conduct a feasibility study to look into the Japanese model of disaster management.
“In Japan, they have a specific law that enables a special council to manage disasters before and when they occur,” he said in Tokyo after a briefing by the Japanese Authority on Disaster Management and Counter-measure Policies.
Muhyiddin was in Japan for the UN World Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction.
Earlier, the Prime Minister told Parliament that there was no plan to set up a Royal Commission of Inquiry with regard to the management of the floods which severely affected several states late last year.
“The inquiry is not necessary,” he said when replying to Azalina Othman (BN-Pengerang).
Measures that had been taken to assist the states and flood victims included an initial allocation of RM500mil, RM787mil under the National Security Council fund and RM893mil under Budget 2015 for flood mitigation projects, he added.
Najib also urged the states that were flooded to adopt sustainable development to cover mining, land clearing and logging.
